newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria kills 18 in underground hideout - paper.
newsitem.headline: Algeria kills 18 in underground hideout - paper.

text.p: Algerian security forces killed 18 Moslem rebels when they stormed a hideout which the guerrillas had dug underneath some greenhouses on a farm, an Algerian newspaper said on Sunday.

The French-language daily Liberte said the guerrillas, who were killed on Saturday at Haouch el Mekhfi village, south of Algiers, were believed to be a splinter group from the Armed Islamic Group (GIA).
Most of the guerrillas were veterans of Afghanistan's Moslem fundamentalist Mujahideen war in the 1980s, Liberte said.
Security forces recovered more than 15 automatic pistols, two assault rifles and some home-made grenades in the rebel hideout, it added.
Three other guerrillas were killed by security forces on Saturday near a cemetery in Beni-Messous district, at the northen edge of Algiers, said Liberte.
Algerian government forces have been locked in conflict for nearly five years with Moslem guerrillas trying to topple the North African country's secular leaders.

About 60,000 people, most of them Moslem militants and security forces members, have died in Algeria's violence since early 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election which radical Islamists were set to win.
